    RectangleIntegral' (f x) (-c - c * I - 1) (c + c * I - 1) = -x⁻¹
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT (by linarith : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2), diffBddAtNegOne xpos]
  intro c hc bddAbove
  obtain ⟨cpos, _⟩ := hc
  have h_mem {s : ℂ} (hs : s ∈ Square (-1) c) :
      -c ≤ s.re + 1 ∧ s.re + 1 ≤ c ∧ -c ≤ s.im ∧ s.im ≤ c := by
    rw [Square, mem_Rect (by simpa using by linarith) (by simp [cpos.le])] at hs
    simpa using hs
  have RectSub : Square (-1) c \ {-1} ⊆ {0, -1}ᶜ := by
    refine fun s ⟨hs, hs1⟩ ↦ not_or.mpr ⟨?_, hs1⟩
    simpa [Complex.ext_iff] using fun _ _ ↦ by linarith [h_mem hs]
  have fHolo : HolomorphicOn (f x) (Square (-1) c \ {-1}) := (isHolomorphicOn xpos).mono RectSub
  have f1Holo :
      HolomorphicOn ((f x) - (fun (s : ℂ) ↦ -x⁻¹ / (s + 1))) (Square (-1) c \ {-1}) := by
    refine fHolo.sub <| (differentiableOn_const _).neg.div ?_
      fun x hx ↦ sPlusOneNeZero hx.2

# A holomorphic lift of one observable rectangular Weil tail forces RH

- **ID:** `ccm-observable-tail-holomorphic-continuation-rh-criterion`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean) / TOP-DOWN BRIDGE
- **Scientific status:** `[FORMALIZATION] [NOT AN RH PROOF] [NOVELTY UNASSESSED]`
- **Statement:** If, for one fixed positive rectangular width and one admissible finite cutoff, the
  ordinary Dirichlet series of the observable logarithmic Weil tail admits an independent
  holomorphic continuation to `Re s > 1`, then RH holds.

## Goal

Replace the internally Xi-defined meromorphic continuation by a genuine continuation property of
one scalar coefficient sequence.  The resulting chain is

```text
independent holomorphic lift of one observable rectangular Weil tail on Re s > 1
  -> full-order divisibility of the Xi-cancelled carrier at every right Xi zero
  -> contradiction with its exact multiplicity-minus-one order
  -> no right Xi zero
  -> RH.
```

The holomorphic lift is allowed to agree with the ordinary Dirichlet series only on an arbitrary
far-right half-plane.  No Xi zero location, real-rootedness, or positivity assumption occurs in the
lift property.

## Theorem

The Lean module
`GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.CCM.CCMRectangularObservableHolomorphicCriterion` defines

```text
XiRectangularWeilTailHolomorphicContinuation L N
```

as the existence of a function analytic on `Re s > 1` which agrees with the ordinary tail
L-series for all sufficiently large real parts.  It proves

```text
riemannHypothesis_of_xiRectangularWeilTailHolomorphicContinuation
```

for every `L>0` and every cutoff `N` beyond which `1<=n` and `L<=log(n)/2`.

## Proof

Let `F` be the independent holomorphic lift.  Subtract the entire finite-prefix series and the
bounded-remainder L-series, then divide by two.  This produces a function `A` analytic on
`Re s>1`.  On a far-right half-plane, the observable-tail identity gives

```text
xiRectangularCancelledSeries L s = xi(s-1/2) * A(s).
```

Both sides are analytic on the connected half-plane, so analytic continuation propagates the
identity throughout `Re s>1`.  If a right Xi zero has multiplicity `m`, the product on the right
has analytic order at least `m`.  The exact cancellation theorem gives order `m-1` on the left.
This contradiction excludes every right Xi zero, hence proves RH.

## Boundary

The present Lean coefficient `xiRectangularWeilLogCoefficient` is the multiplicity-exact
zero-side Weil polarization.  Therefore this theorem is a completed divisor-observable bridge,
not yet an unconditional source proof.  The remaining positive producer is:

```text
derive the independent Re s>1 holomorphic lift from the completed prime--Gamma /
critical-Mellin formula for the same rectangular two-edge values.
```

That producer must not define its continuation through the Xi divisor or assume any equivalent
zero-locus, anti-Herglotz, or limiting-positive-measure condition.

# Harmonic ∘ holomorphic is harmonic

A general transport lemma, not specific to the Böttcher setting: precomposing a harmonic function
with a holomorphic map yields a harmonic function. The mechanism is the local holomorphic primitive
(`HarmonicOnNhd.exists_analyticOnNhd_ball_re_eq`): a harmonic `g` equals `Re F` for a holomorphic
`F` on a ball; then `g ∘ f = Re (F ∘ f)` with `F ∘ f` holomorphic, whose real part is harmonic.

This is the law that extends the near-`∞` dynamical Green's function down the whole basin: writing
`G_c = 2⁻ⁿ · (G_c ∘ f_c^[n])`, harmonicity on the escape region propagates through every holomorphic
iterate `f_c^[n]` to the full exterior `Ω_c` — the domain where the natural-boundary (connected

import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.Analytic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Constructions

open Complex InnerProductSpace Metric Topology

/-- **Harmonic ∘ holomorphic is harmonic.** If `g : ℂ → ℝ` is harmonic at `f x` and `f : ℂ → ℂ`
is analytic (holomorphic) at `x`, then `g ∘ f` is harmonic at `x`. -/
theorem HarmonicAt.comp_analytic {g : ℂ → ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {x : ℂ}
    (hg : HarmonicAt g (f x)) (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f x) :
    HarmonicAt (g ∘ f) x := by
  have hmem : {y | HarmonicAt g y} ∈ 𝓝 (f x) := (isOpen_setOf_harmonicAt g).mem_nhds hg
  obtain ⟨R, hR, hRsub⟩ := Metric.mem_nhds_iff.1 hmem
  have hgball : HarmonicOnNhd g (ball (f x) R) := fun y hy => hRsub hy
  obtain ⟨F, hFan, hFeq⟩ :=
    InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.exists_analyticOnNhd_ball_re_eq hgball
  have hcomp : AnalyticAt ℂ (F ∘ f) x := (hFan (f x) (mem_ball_self hR)).comp hf
  have hharm : HarmonicAt (fun y => ((F ∘ f) y).re) x := AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_re hcomp
  have hpre : f ⁻¹' (ball (f x) R) ∈ 𝓝 x :=
    hf.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds (ball_mem_nhds _ hR)
  have heq : (fun y => ((F ∘ f) y).re) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (g ∘ f) := by
    filter_upwards [hpre] with y hy
    simp only [Function.comp_apply]; exact hFeq hy
  exact (harmonicAt_congr_nhds heq).mp hharm

/-- `HarmonicOnNhd` version: `g` harmonic near `f '' s` and `f` analytic on `s` ⟹ `g ∘ f` harmonic

theorem HarmonicOnNhd.comp_analytic {g : ℂ → ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : Set ℂ}

    HarmonicOnNhd (g ∘ f) s :=
  fun x hx => HarmonicAt.comp_analytic (hg x hx) (hf x hx)

# Slice holomorphy of the transverse Laplacian

The iteration integrates the step operator, and slice holomorphy passes through the integral; so what
remains is that the step operator itself is slice holomorphic. Its potential term is, being a product
of slice holomorphic functions. Its transverse Laplacian is the point of this file.

Along the coordinate being differentiated the statement is one-variable: the second partial
derivative restricted to that slice is the second derivative of the slice, and the derivative of a
holomorphic function is holomorphic.

Along a *different* coordinate the two variables are genuinely separate, and the argument is the
Cauchy representation: the second derivative in one coordinate is a contour integral of the function,
the integrand is holomorphic in the other coordinate, and holomorphy passes through the contour
integral by the one-variable statement already available.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set Complex Metric

variable {k : ℕ}

/-- Along the coordinate being differentiated, the second partial derivative is the second
derivative of the slice. -/
theorem cpartial_cpartial_update_same (i : Fin k) (w : (Fin k → ℂ) → ℂ) (z : Fin k → ℂ)
    (ζ : ℂ) :
    cpartial i (cpartial i w) (Function.update z i ζ)
      = deriv (deriv fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update z i ξ)) ζ := by
  have hfun : (fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update (Function.update z i ζ) i ξ))
      = fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update z i ξ) := by
    funext ξ
    rw [Function.update_idem]
  rw [cpartial_cpartial_eq, Function.update_self, hfun]

/-- Along a different coordinate, the second partial derivative is the second derivative of the
slice at the shifted point. -/
theorem cpartial_cpartial_update_other {i j : Fin k} (hij : i ≠ j) (w : (Fin k → ℂ) → ℂ)
    (z : Fin k → ℂ) (ζ : ℂ) :
    cpartial i (cpartial i w) (Function.update z j ζ)
      = deriv (deriv fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update (Function.update z i ξ) j ζ)) (z i) := by
  have hfun : (fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update (Function.update z j ζ) i ξ))
      = fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update (Function.update z i ξ) j ζ) := by
    funext ξ
    rw [Function.update_comm (Ne.symm hij)]
  rw [cpartial_cpartial_eq, Function.update_of_ne hij, hfun]

/-- **Slice holomorphy of the second partial derivative along the same coordinate**, on the same
tube: in one variable the derivative of a holomorphic function is holomorphic on the same open set. -/
theorem sliceHolo_cpartial_cpartial_same {ρ' : ℝ} {w : (Fin k → ℂ) → ℂ}
    (hwh : SliceHolo w ρ') (i : Fin k) {z : Fin k → ℂ} (hz : z ∈ tube k ρ') :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun ζ : ℂ => cpartial i (cpartial i w) (Function.update z i ζ))
      (imStrip ρ') := by
  have hopen := isOpen_imStrip ρ'
  have hslice : DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update z i ξ)) (imStrip ρ') :=
    hwh z hz i
  have hana : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (fun ξ : ℂ => w (Function.update z i ξ)) (imStrip ρ') :=

/-!
# Endpoint-holomorphic Real-corona smoothness

This file isolates the analytic condition needed for an upper/lower CRT idempotent to lie in an
endpoint-holomorphic subalgebra.  A representative must be holomorphic on one connected
neighborhood containing the compactifying endpoints and take the constant values `1` and `0` on
the two divisor sectors.

The classification is exact.  Finite separated sectors admit an explicit Lagrange-polynomial
representative.  If either infinite sector accumulates at an endpoint inside the holomorphic
domain, the identity theorem makes the requested two values incompatible.  Thus, under the
two endpoint-accumulation hypotheses, endpoint-holomorphic representability is equivalent to
finiteness of both sectors.
-/

open Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-- An upper/lower corona separator represented by a function holomorphic through the chosen
endpoint neighborhood. -/
def HasEndpointHolomorphicCoronaRepresentative
    (U upper lower : Set ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ,
    AnalyticOnNhd ℂ h U ∧
    (∀ z ∈ upper, h z = 1) ∧
    (∀ z ∈ lower, h z = 0)

/-- Natural endpoint-holomorphic coefficient algebra on a divisor `Z`: functions on `Z` which
are restrictions of holomorphic functions on `U`. -/
def endpointHolomorphicSubalgebra (U Z : Set ℂ) : Subalgebra ℂ (Z → ℂ) where
  carrier := {f | ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticOnNhd ℂ h U ∧
    ∀ z : Z, h (z : ℂ) = f z}
  zero_mem' := ⟨fun _ => 0, analyticOnNhd_const, by simp⟩
  add_mem' := by
    rintro f g ⟨hf, hfA, hfeq⟩ ⟨hg, hgA, hgeq⟩
    refine ⟨fun z => hf z + hg z, hfA.add hgA, ?_⟩
    intro z
    simp [hfeq z, hgeq z]
  one_mem' := ⟨fun _ => 1, analyticOnNhd_const, by simp⟩
  mul_mem' := by
    rintro f g ⟨hf, hfA, hfeq⟩ ⟨hg, hgA, hgeq⟩
    refine ⟨fun z => hf z * hg z, hfA.mul hgA, ?_⟩
    intro z
    simp [hfeq z, hgeq z]
  algebraMap_mem' := by
    intro c
    refine ⟨fun _ => c, analyticOnNhd_const, ?_⟩
    intro z
    rfl

/-- The endpoint-holomorphic coefficient algebra is dense in the full divisor function algebra for
pointwise convergence.  The proof is stronger than approximation: every basic finite-coordinate
condition is met exactly by a Lagrange polynomial. -/
theorem endpointHolomorphicSubalgebra_dense (U Z : Set ℂ) :
    Dense (endpointHolomorphicSubalgebra U Z : Set (Z → ℂ)) := by
  rw [dense_iff_closure_eq, Set.eq_univ_iff_forall]
  intro f
  rw [mem_closure_iff]
  intro o ho hfo
  classical
  have hnhds : o ∈ nhds f := ho.mem_nhds hfo
  rw [nhds_pi, Filter.mem_pi'] at hnhds
  rcases hnhds with ⟨I, t, ht, hto⟩
  let p : Polynomial ℂ := Lagrange.interpolate I (fun z : Z => (z : ℂ)) f
  let g : Z → ℂ := fun z => p.eval (z : ℂ)
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun z : Z => (z : ℂ)) (I : Set Z) := by
    intro a _ b _ hab
    exact Subtype.ext hab
  have hmatch : ∀ z ∈ I, g z = f z := by
    intro z hz
    simpa [g, p] using Lagrange.eval_interpolate_at_node f hinj hz
  have hgmem : g ∈ endpointHolomorphicSubalgebra U Z := by
    refine ⟨fun z => p.eval z,
      (AnalyticOnNhd.eval_polynomial p).mono (Set.subset_univ U), ?_⟩
    intro z
    rfl
  refine ⟨g, hto ?_, hgmem⟩
  intro z hz
  rw [hmatch z hz]
  exact mem_of_mem_nhds (ht z)

/-- Upper-sector characteristic function on the complete two-sector divisor. -/
noncomputable def endpointRealCoronaIdempotent
    (upper lower : Set ℂ) : (upper ∪ lower : Set ℂ) → ℂ :=
  fun z => @ite ℂ ((z : ℂ) ∈ upper) (Classical.propDecidable _) 1 0

/-- The upper-sector characteristic function is an idempotent in the full divisor function
algebra, without any finiteness or regularity hypothesis. -/
theorem endpointRealCoronaIdempotent_isIdempotent (upper lower : Set ℂ) :
    IsIdempotentElem (endpointRealCoronaIdempotent upper lower) := by
  classical
  funext z
  simp only [endpointRealCoronaIdempotent, Pi.mul_apply]
  split_ifs <;> norm_num

/-- Membership of the Real-corona idempotent in the natural endpoint-holomorphic coefficient
algebra is exactly endpoint-holomorphic representability of its upper/lower values. -/
theorem endpointRealCoronaIdempotent_mem_iff
    {U upper lower : Set ℂ} (hdisj : Disjoint upper lower) :
    endpointRealCoronaIdempotent upper lower ∈
        endpointHolomorphicSubalgebra U (upper ∪ lower) ↔
      HasEndpointHolomorphicCoronaRepresentative U upper lower := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h, hA, heq⟩
    refine ⟨h, hA, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro z hz
      have hzcarrier : z ∈ upper ∪ lower := Or.inl hz
      have heval := heq ⟨z, hzcarrier⟩
      simpa [endpointRealCoronaIdempotent, hz] using heval
    · intro z hz
      have hzcarrier : z ∈ upper ∪ lower := Or.inr hz
      have hnot : z ∉ upper := fun hzu => Set.disjoint_left.1 hdisj hzu hz
      have heval := heq ⟨z, hzcarrier⟩

/-!
# Fixed-fiber Kramers symmetry is rigid in a holomorphic parameter

A standard two-dimensional antiunitary Kramers symmetry forces a matrix into quaternionic form

`[[a, b], [-conj b, conj a]]`.

If all four entries depend holomorphically on the same complex parameter, the conjugate partners
are holomorphic too. The open mapping theorem then makes `a` and `b` constant. Consequently the
whole family and its determinant are constant.

Thus a nonconstant holomorphic determinant cannot obtain off-real local multiplicity doubling from
a fixed antiunitary symmetry acting within every parameter fiber. The nonconstant alternative is
parameter-reversing covariance, relating `s` to `conj s`; that pairs distinct off-real fibers and
does not impose even analytic order at either point.
-/

open Complex Set

namespace RHTower

/-- If a holomorphic function and its pointwise complex conjugate are both holomorphic on a
connected open set, the function is constant there. -/
theorem holomorphic_conjugate_pair_constant
    {U : Set ℂ} {f g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUconn : IsConnected U)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f U) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g U)
    (hpair : ∀ z ∈ U, g z = starRingEnd ℂ (f z)) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, ∀ z ∈ U, f z = c := by
  have hsum : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (fun z => f z + g z) U := hf.add hg
  have him : ∀ z ∈ U, ((f z + g z).im : ℝ) = 0 := by
    intro z hz
    rw [hpair z hz]
    simp
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hsum.eq_const_of_im_eq_const him hUopen hUconn
  obtain ⟨z₀, hz₀⟩ := hUconn.nonempty
  have hre : ∀ z ∈ U, (f z).re = (f z₀).re := by
    intro z hz
    have hzC := congrArg Complex.re (hC z hz)
    have hz₀C := congrArg Complex.re (hC z₀ hz₀)
    rw [hpair z hz] at hzC
    rw [hpair z₀ hz₀] at hz₀C
    simp only [Complex.add_re, Complex.conj_re] at hzC hz₀C
    linarith
  exact hf.eq_const_of_re_eq_const hre hUopen hUconn

/-- A same-fiber holomorphic standard Kramers two-by-two family is constant. -/
theorem holomorphic_standardKramers_twoByTwo_constant
    {U : Set ℂ} {a b c d : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUconn : IsConnected U)
    (ha : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ a U) (hb : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ b U)
    (hc : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ c U) (hd : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ d U)
    (hdiag : ∀ z ∈ U, d z = starRingEnd ℂ (a z))
    (hoff : ∀ z ∈ U, c z = -starRingEnd ℂ (b z)) :
    ∃ a₀ b₀ : ℂ, ∀ z ∈ U,
      a z = a₀ ∧ b z = b₀ ∧ c z = -starRingEnd ℂ b₀ ∧ d z = starRingEnd ℂ a₀ := by
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀⟩ := holomorphic_conjugate_pair_constant hUopen hUconn ha hd hdiag
  have hnegc : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (fun z => -c z) U := hc.neg
  have hpairb : ∀ z ∈ U, -c z = starRingEnd ℂ (b z) := by
    intro z hz
    rw [hoff z hz]
    simp
  obtain ⟨b₀, hb₀⟩ :=
    holomorphic_conjugate_pair_constant hUopen hUconn hb hnegc hpairb
  refine ⟨a₀, b₀, fun z hz => ⟨ha₀ z hz, hb₀ z hz, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · rw [hoff z hz, hb₀ z hz]
  · rw [hdiag z hz, ha₀ z hz]

/-- The determinant of a same-fiber holomorphic standard Kramers family is constant. -/
theorem holomorphic_standardKramers_twoByTwo_det_constant
    {U : Set ℂ} {a b c d : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUconn : IsConnected U)
    (ha : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ a U) (hb : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ b U)
    (hc : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ c U) (hd : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ d U)
    (hdiag : ∀ z ∈ U, d z = starRingEnd ℂ (a z))
    (hoff : ∀ z ∈ U, c z = -starRingEnd ℂ (b z)) :
    ∃ D : ℂ, ∀ z ∈ U, a z * d z - b z * c z = D := by
  obtain ⟨a₀, b₀, hconst⟩ := holomorphic_standardKramers_twoByTwo_constant
    hUopen hUconn ha hb hc hd hdiag hoff
  refine ⟨a₀ * starRingEnd ℂ a₀ + b₀ * starRingEnd ℂ b₀, fun z hz => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨haeq, hbeq, hceq, hdeq⟩ := hconst z hz
  rw [haeq, hbeq, hceq, hdeq]
  ring

end RHTower

/-! ### The facet-codimension law for constant-multiplier data -/

/-- **A constant-multiplier facet datum.**  `ℚ`-independent translation steps together with, for
every facet, an entire hypertranscendental carrier which each omitted translation reproduces up to a
constant factor.  Taking all multipliers `1` recovers the invariant datum
`ScalarFacetRealization`. -/
structure QuasiPeriodFacetRealization (V : Finset α) (facets : Set (Finset α)) where
  /-- The translation steps attached to the vertices. -/
  ω : α → ℂ
  /-- The steps are `ℚ`-linearly independent. -/
  indep : LinearIndependent ℚ ω
  /-- The facet carriers. -/
  carrier : Finset α → (ℂ → ℂ)
  /-- Each carrier is entire. -/
  carrier_entire : ∀ F ∈ facets, Differentiable ℂ (carrier F)
  /-- Each omitted translation reproduces the carrier up to a constant multiplier. -/
  carrier_multiplier : ∀ F ∈ facets, ∀ v ∈ V \ F,
    ∃ a : ℂ, ∀ z, carrier F (z + ω v) = a * carrier F z
  /-- Each carrier is hypertranscendental. -/
  carrier_hypertranscendental : ∀ F ∈ facets, Hypertranscendental (carrier F)

/-- An entire invariant datum is the constant-multiplier datum with all multipliers `1`. -/
def ScalarFacetRealization.toQuasiPeriod {V : Finset α} {facets : Set (Finset α)}
    (R : ScalarFacetRealization V facets)
    (hentire : ∀ F ∈ facets, Differentiable ℂ (R.carrier F)) :
    QuasiPeriodFacetRealization V facets where
  ω := R.ω
  indep := R.indep
  carrier := R.carrier
  carrier_entire := hentire
  carrier_multiplier := fun F hF v hv =>
    ⟨1, fun z => by rw [R.carrier_periodic F hF v hv z, one_mul]⟩
  carrier_hypertranscendental := R.carrier_hypertranscendental

/-!
# Full-period extraction

The full period group of a function on a finite-dimensional space,

`translationPeriods G = {h | forall z, G (z + h) = G z}`,

is a closed additive subgroup whenever `G` is continuous, so the line-direction structure theorem
applies to it verbatim: `G` has a linear space of directions along which it is constant, and modulo
that space its periods are separated.

When `G` is entire on a complex space the linear part is automatically a **complex** subspace, not
merely a real one.  A real line of periods through a direction `x` makes the entire one-variable
restriction `w -> G (z + w • x)` constant on the real axis, and the identity theorem then makes it
constant on all of `C`.  This is exactly the classical statement that the identity component of the
period group of a holomorphic function is complex-linear.
-/

open Filter Topology Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {V : Type*} {W : Type*}

/-- The full group of translation periods of a function. -/
def translationPeriods [AddCommGroup V] (G : V → W) : AddSubgroup V where
  carrier := {h | Function.Periodic G h}
  zero_mem' := by intro z; simp
  add_mem' := fun ha hb => Function.Periodic.add_period ha hb
  neg_mem' := fun ha => Function.Periodic.neg ha

@[simp]
theorem mem_translationPeriods [AddCommGroup V] {G : V → W} {h : V} :
    h ∈ translationPeriods G ↔ ∀ z, G (z + h) = G z := Iff.rfl

/-- In one complex variable this is the corpus period subgroup. -/
theorem translationPeriods_eq_periodSubgroup (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    translationPeriods f = periodSubgroup f := rfl

/-- **The full period group of a continuous function is closed.** -/
theorem isClosed_translationPeriods [AddCommGroup V] [TopologicalSpace V]
    [IsTopologicalAddGroup V] [TopologicalSpace W] [T2Space W]
    {G : V → W} (hG : Continuous G) :
    IsClosed ((translationPeriods G : AddSubgroup V) : Set V) := by
  have hset : ((translationPeriods G : AddSubgroup V) : Set V)
      = ⋂ z : V, {h : V | G (z + h) = G z} := by
    ext h
    simp only [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_translationPeriods, Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  rw [hset]
  refine isClosed_iInter fun z => ?_
  have hcont : Continuous fun h : V => G (z + h) := hG.comp (continuous_const.add continuous_id)
  exact isClosed_eq hcont continuous_const

variable [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V]

/-- **The linear period directions of an entire function are complex.**  A real line of periods in
direction `x` restricts `G` to a constant on the real axis of the complex line through `x`, and the
identity theorem propagates that to the whole line. -/
theorem complex_smul_mem_lineDirections_translationPeriods
    {G : V → ℂ} (hG : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ G Set.univ) {x : V}
    (hx : x ∈ lineDirections (translationPeriods G)) (w : ℂ) :
    w • x ∈ lineDirections (translationPeriods G) := by
  -- It suffices to show every complex multiple of `x` is a period.
  have key : ∀ v : ℂ, ∀ z : V, G (z + v • x) = G z := by
    intro v z
    set L : ℂ →L[ℂ] V := (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ ℂ).smulRight x with hL
    have hLapply : ∀ u : ℂ, L u = u • x := by
      intro u
      rw [hL]
      simp
    set f : ℂ → ℂ := fun u => G (z + L u) - G z with hf
    have hfa : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f Set.univ := by
      have haff : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (fun u : ℂ => z + L u) Set.univ :=
        analyticOnNhd_const.add (L.analyticOnNhd Set.univ)
      have hcomp : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (fun u : ℂ => G (z + L u)) Set.univ :=
        (hG.comp haff) fun u _ => Set.mem_univ _
      exact hcomp.sub analyticOnNhd_const
    have hcast : ∀ (r : ℝ) (y : V), ((r : ℂ)) • y = r • y := by
      intro r y
      rw [← Complex.coe_algebraMap, algebraMap_smul]
    have hreal : ∀ t : ℝ, f (t : ℂ) = 0 := by
      intro t
      have hper : G (z + (t : ℝ) • x) = G z := hx t z
      rw [hf]
      simp only [hLapply, hcast, hper, sub_self]
    have hfreq : ∃ᶠ u in 𝓝[≠] (0 : ℂ), f u = 0 := by
      have htend : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)) atTop (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℂ)) := by
        refine tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within _ ?_ ?_
        · have h : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (1 / (n + 1 : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 (0 : ℝ)) :=
            tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
          have h2 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)) atTop
              (𝓝 (((0 : ℝ) : ℂ))) := (Complex.continuous_ofReal.tendsto (0 : ℝ)).comp h
          rwa [Complex.ofReal_zero] at h2
        · filter_upwards with n
          simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) := by positivity
          exact Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr hpos.ne'
      exact htend.frequently (Frequently.of_forall fun n => hreal _)
    have hzero : Set.EqOn f 0 Set.univ :=
      hfa.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq_zero isPreconnected_univ
        (Set.mem_univ _) hfreq
